mainTopic: Vows made על דעת רבים, why witnesses sign a גט מפני תיקון העולם, and how הלל's פרוסבול works
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about making a כהן take a vow that cannot easily be undone. The גמרא settles on a vow made על דעת רבים, which אמימר rules cannot be undone. It then adds a limit: such a vow can be undone for a דבר מצוה, as in the story of the children's teacher whom רבינא brought back. Next, the גמרא asks how the משנה can call witnesses signing a גט a rabbinic fix (תיקון העולם) when signing seems to come from the Torah. רבה answers that the משנה follows רבי אלעזר, for whom the signatures are only a rabbinic backup. רב יוסף answers that the fix was making witnesses write out their full names, as רבן גמליאל taught, and the גמרא explains why great rabbis could still sign with a well-known mark. Finally, the גמרא turns to הלל's פרוסבול and asks how a rabbinic enactment can stop שביעית from cancelling debts. אביי answers that nowadays, according to רבי, cancelling debts is only rabbinic, because it depends on the release of land.

steps.title: The vow is administered in public
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier question: we make the כהן take his vow in front of many people.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have him take the vow in public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question from just before this section: how can we be sure this כהן's vow will not simply be undone? It says the vow is made publicly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow can normally be undone by a חכם (התרת נדרים). The idea here is that a vow taken ברבים, in front of many people, is harder or impossible to undo, so it is a reliable safeguard.

keyTerms.meaning: we make him vow / we administer a vow
in public, in front of many people

phrases.english: That we administer the vow to him in public.
phrases.notes: "Him" is the כהן from the discussion just before this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question from the previous part of the daf about how to keep the vow from being undone.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical safeguard: making the vow in public
steps.terutzMaskana: A vow made ברבים is treated as hard to undo.

steps.title: But some say even a public vow can be undone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: it only works for the view that a public vow cannot be undone, not for the view that it can.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says a vow made in public cannot be undone. But for the one who says it can be undone, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 1. There is a מחלוקת whether a נדר שהודר ברבים can be undone, and the answer only fits one side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a public vow can still be undone (יש לו הפרה), then making the כהן vow publicly gives no real protection. So the answer in Step 1 is not enough for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: this works well for the one who says
a vow that was made in public
undoing/cancelling (here: having a חכם release the vow)

phrases.english: This works out well according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: נֶדֶר שֶׁהוּדַּר בְּרַבִּים – אֵין לוֹ הֲפָרָה;
phrases.english: a vow made in public has no undoing;
phrases.notes: "Undoing" here means a חכם releasing the vow, not a husband or father cancelling it.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר יֵשׁ לוֹ הֲפָרָה,
phrases.english: but according to the one who says it does have undoing,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a public vow is a safe guarantee
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the view that a public vow can be undone, a public vow offers no protection, so the answer fails for that view.

steps.title: The vow is made based on the public's consent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the vow is made 'על דעת רבים', based on the consent of the public, which is stronger than just public.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have him vow based on the consent of the public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a stronger answer: the כהן vows על דעת רבים, meaning the vow depends on the agreement of many people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ברבים' only means many people were present. 'על דעת רבים' means the vow is tied to the will of the public. Undoing it would need everyone's agreement, which is practically impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: based on the consent of the public

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'ברבים' (in public) with 'על דעת רבים' (on the public's consent). The second is a stronger kind of vow.

phrases.english: That we administer the vow to him based on the consent of the public –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 2 by upgrading the kind of vow.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between two kinds of vow
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A public vow, which some say can be undone, is the safeguard.
steps.terutzMaskana: The safeguard is a vow על דעת רבים, which even that view agrees cannot be undone.

steps.title: אמימר rules a vow on the public's consent cannot be undone
steps.stepSummary: The answer is backed up by אמימר's ruling that even those who allow undoing a public vow agree that a vow על דעת רבים cannot be undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: As אמימר said: the הלכה is that even according to the one who says a vow made in public can be undone, a vow made on the public's consent cannot be undone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the answer in Step 3 from a ruling of אמימר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמימר shows that the two kinds of vow really are different. Even the lenient view agrees about על דעת רבים, so the answer works for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא whose ruling is quoted
even according to the one who says

steps.whatToRemember: A vow על דעת רבים cannot be undone, even according to the view that a vow made ברבים can be undone.

phrases.english: As Ameimar said, the halakha is:
Even according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: נֶדֶר שֶׁהוּדַּר בְּרַבִּים יֵשׁ לוֹ הֲפָרָה,
phrases.english: a vow made in public can be undone,

phrases.aramaic: עַל דַּעַת רַבִּים – אֵין לוֹ הֲפָרָה.
phrases.english: one made on the consent of the public cannot be undone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 3 with a ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That a vow על דעת רבים cannot be undone even according to the lenient view

steps.title: Exception: such a vow can be undone for a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the rule: a vow על דעת רבים cannot be undone only for an optional matter, but it can be undone for a דבר מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only to an optional matter, but for a matter of a מצוה it can be undone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to אמימר's rule. When undoing the vow is needed for a מצוה, it can be undone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strong vow stays locked when the reason to undo it is only personal and optional (דבר הרשות). When releasing it is needed for a מצוה, the release is allowed. This is an exception to the rule. It does not cancel the rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical limit on vows על דעת רבים: they are binding except when releasing them is needed for a מצוה.

phrases.english: And this applies to an optional matter,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לִדְבַר מִצְוָה – יֵשׁ לוֹ הֲפָרָה.
phrases.english: but for a matter of a מצוה – it can be undone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies אמימר's ruling from Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow על דעת רבים can be undone when needed for a דבר מצוה.

steps.title: The story of the children's teacher
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא made a careless teacher vow על דעת רבים to stop teaching, but רבינא undid the vow and brought him back because no one as careful could be found.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like that teacher of children whom רב אחא made vow on the public's consent, because he was careless with the children. רבינא brought him back, because no one was found who was as careful as he was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the exception from Step 5 with a real case. Teaching children Torah is a מצוה, so the vow was undone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow was made על דעת רבים, which normally cannot be undone. But teaching children is a דבר מצוה, and he was the most careful teacher available. So רבינא released the vow and reinstated him.
steps.whatToRemember: A vow על דעת רבים is binding, but it can be undone when releasing it is needed for a מצוה, as with the teacher of children.

phrases.english: Like that teacher of young children

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַדְּרֵיהּ רַב אַחָא עַל דַּעַת רַבִּים,
phrases.english: whom Rav Aḥa made vow on the consent of the public,
phrases.notes: The vow was that he would stop teaching.

phrases.english: because he was negligent with the children;
and Ravina brought him back,
because no one was found who was as careful as he was.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the exception of Step 5 with a case.
steps.raayaObject: That a vow על דעת רבים can be undone for a דבר מצוה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of רב אחא, רבינא and the children's teacher

steps.title: New line of the משנה: witnesses sign the גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: witnesses sign the גט because of תיקון העולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה taught: and the witnesses sign the גט for the betterment of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the next part of the משנה. It is setting up a question on this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists this among the rabbinic enactments made מפני תיקון העולם. The גמרא will now ask whether that label really fits.

keyTerms.meaning: the betterment of the world; a rabbinic fix for society

phrases.english: And the witnesses sign the bill of divorce
for the betterment of the world:

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָעֵדִים חוֹתְמִין עַל הַגֵּט מִפְּנֵי תִּיקּוּן הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses sign the גט because of תיקון העולם.

steps.title: Signing is already required by the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: how can signing be a rabbinic fix, when the פסוק already shows that documents are signed by witnesses?
steps.simpleTranslation: For the betterment of the world?! It is from the Torah, as it is written: 'and write it in the document and sign it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's reason. If witnesses signing is already from the Torah, why call it a rabbinic תיקון העולם?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תיקון העולם is something the חכמים added. The גמרא brings a פסוק showing that documents are signed, so it seems to be דאורייתא. That would make the משנה's label wrong, and the גמרא will need to explain it.

phrases.english: For the betterment of the world?!
It is by Torah law, as it is written:
"And write in the deed, and sign"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in the משנה line quoted in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that witnesses sign the גט מפני תיקון העולם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק shows that signing documents is דאורייתא, so it cannot be just a rabbinic enactment.

steps.title: רבה: The משנה follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the משנה follows רבי אלעזר, who holds that the witnesses to the handing over make the divorce. Signing witnesses are only a rabbinic addition, in case the handing-over witnesses die or move overseas.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: The rule is needed according to רבי אלעזר, who says the witnesses who watch the handing over are what make the divorce. The Rabbis added signing witnesses to make things work better, because sometimes the witnesses die, or sometimes they move overseas.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question from step 8. He says the משנה follows רבי אלעזר, and for him, signing witnesses really are only a rabbinic fix.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר, the Torah only needs witnesses who watch the husband hand over the גט, so a signature is not needed by Torah law. The Rabbis added signatures as a backup. If the handing-over witnesses die or go far away, the גט can still be confirmed by checking the signatures. This makes the משנה's word 'fix' fit perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (a specific case or opinion)
Witnesses who watch the handing over of the גט
They 'cut', meaning they make the divorce take effect

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אלעזר wants a גט with no signatures. For him the signatures are required by the Rabbis. They just are not what makes the divorce work by Torah law.

phrases.english: Rabba said: It is needed
according to Rabbi Elazar, who says:
the witnesses of the handing over make the divorce;
the Rabbis instituted signing witnesses
for the betterment of the world
because sometimes the witnesses die,

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי זִימְנִין דְּאָזְלִי לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם.
phrases.english: or else, sometimes they go overseas.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: לָא צְרִיכָא – לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the משנה to a particular תנא (רבי אלעזר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Signing is required by the Torah, so it cannot be called a rabbinic fix
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי אלעזר, handing-over witnesses make the divorce, so the signatures are a rabbinic backup

steps.title: רב יוסף: Even רבי מאיר agrees, because the fix was writing full names
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a different answer. The משנה can follow even רבי מאיר, and the rabbinic fix was that witnesses must write out their full names on a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: You can even say the משנה follows רבי מאיר. The fix was that the witnesses must clearly write out their names in a גט, for the betterment of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a second answer to the question from step 8. He explains the משנה's 'fix' in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that the signing witnesses are what make the divorce, so signing itself cannot be a rabbinic fix for him. רב יוסף says the fix was not the signing itself. It was the added rule that witnesses must clearly write out their full names. This way the משנה fits even רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who holds that the signing witnesses make the divorce
They clearly write out their names

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: You can even say it follows Rabbi Meir,
they instituted that the witnesses
must clearly write out their names on bills of divorce
for the betterment of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 8, different from רבה's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets what the fix in the משנה was
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fix must be the signing itself, which only works for רבי אלעזר
steps.terutzMaskana: The fix was writing out full names, so the משנה fits even רבי מאיר

steps.title: The old practice: witnesses signed without full names
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes the old way: a witness wrote only 'I, so-and-so, signed as a witness.' The גט was valid only if his handwriting could be matched to another document.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: At first, a witness would write 'I, so-and-so, signed as a witness.' If his handwriting could be found somewhere else, the גט was valid. If not, it was invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב יוסף. This part sets up the problem that the fix solved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the old days, witnesses did not write clear identifying names. So the only way to confirm a signature was to find the same handwriting on another document. If no match turned up, the גט was invalid. That was a real problem, and it is the background for the תקנה in the next step.

phrases.english: As it is taught: At first, he would write
"I, so-and-so, signed as a witness";

phrases.aramaic: אִם כְּתַב יָדוֹ יוֹצֵא מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר – כָּשֵׁר,
phrases.english: if his handwriting turns up from another place, it is valid,
phrases.notes: He means: if the same signature can be matched on some other document.

phrases.english: and if not, it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the ברייתא that supports רב יוסף
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim that the fix was writing out full names

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: A great fix that witnesses write full names
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says a great תקנה was made: witnesses must clearly write out their names on a גט, for תיקון העולם. This matches רב יוסף's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said: They made a great fix, that the witnesses must clearly write out their names on bills of divorce, for the betterment of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with רבן גמליאל naming the fix. This completes the proof for רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל uses the exact words of the משנה, 'for the betterment of the world', to describe the rule of writing full names. This shows that the משנה's 'fix' can mean the full-names rule and not the signing itself. With full names, people who know the witnesses can recognize their signatures, so fewer גיטין are lost.

keyTerms.meaning: The נשיא who reports the great fix

steps.whatToRemember: Two answers to why signing a גט is called a 'fix': רבה says that for רבי אלעזר the signatures themselves are rabbinic. רב יוסף says that even for רבי מאיר, the fix was requiring witnesses to write out full names, as רבן גמליאל taught.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: תַּקָּנָה גְּדוֹלָה הִתְקִינוּ,
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said: They instituted a great ordinance,
that they must clearly write out their names on bills of divorce
for the betterment of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: תַּקָּנָה גְּדוֹלָה הִתְקִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 11
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's explanation of the משנה's fix
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבן גמליאל's statement in the ברייתא, using the משנה's own words

steps.title: Great rabbis signed with only a mark
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that witnesses must write full names, because famous אמוראים signed with only a picture or a letter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a mark really not good enough? But רב drew a fish, רבי חנינא drew a palm branch, רב חסדא drew a ס, רב הושעיא drew an ע, and רבה בר רב הונא drew a sail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question on רבן גמליאל's rule from Step 12. Many great rabbis signed with just a symbol, not their full names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said witnesses must clearly write out their names. If so, a picture or a single letter should not be enough. Yet these great אמוראים signed that way, which seems to go against the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A mark or symbol used in place of a full signature

phrases.english: But with a mark, it is not enough?!
phrases.notes: He's asking about רבן גמליאל's rule that a witness must write out his full name.

phrases.english: But Rav drew a fish;
and Rabbi Chanina drew a palm branch;

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא סָמֶךְ; וְרַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא עַיִן;
phrases.english: Rav Chisda drew a samekh; and Rav Hoshaya drew an ayin;

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא צָיֵיר מָכוּתָא!
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna drew a sail!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְסִימָנָא לָא?! וְהָא רַב צָיֵיר כְּוָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the full-name requirement established in Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's rule that witnesses must clearly write their names
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Great אמוראים signed with only symbols, which suggests a mark is enough

steps.title: Everyone knew the rabbis' marks
steps.stepSummary: The rabbis are different, because their marks were well known to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis are different, since people are familiar with their marks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. A famous rabbi's mark is as clear as a full name, because everyone recognizes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the rule is that the signature must be easy to identify. An ordinary person's mark would not be recognized. A great rabbi's well-known mark is, so it serves the same purpose.

phrases.english: The rabbis are different,
since people are familiar with their marks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: well-known marks are as clear as full names
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any mark goes against the full-name rule
steps.terutzMaskana: A mark everyone recognizes is acceptable, so the rule still stands for ordinary people

steps.title: How did the marks first become known
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the rabbis first made their marks known to people.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the start, how did they make their marks known?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. Before anyone knew the marks, the rabbis could not use them on legal documents, so how did people come to know them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said the marks were acceptable because they were famous. But a mark is not famous on day one. The גמרא wants to know how it became familiar without breaking the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: They made them public, spread them

phrases.english: At first, with what did they make them known?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up question on the answer of Step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the rabbis' marks first became widely recognized

steps.title: They first used the marks in letters
steps.stepSummary: They first used their marks in letters, where no legal signature is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: In letters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the rabbis first used their marks on letters. Once people learned them, they could use them on legal documents too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A letter does not need a legal signature, so using a mark there breaks no rule. Over time everyone learned the marks this way. Then the marks became clear enough to use as signatures.
steps.whatToRemember: The full-name rule is about clarity. A great rabbi's mark that everyone already knew from his letters was clear enough.

phrases.english: In letters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The marks were first made known through letters, which need no legal signature

steps.title: Why הלל made the פרוסבול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה and quotes a משנה in שביעית: הלל made the פרוסבול because people stopped lending before שמיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: הלל made the פרוסבול. We learned elsewhere: a פרוסבול is not cancelled by שמיטה. This is one of the things הלל הזקן made. He saw that people stopped lending to each other, and they broke the Torah's command 'Beware that there be no base thought in your heart.' So he made the פרוסבול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the next line of our משנה, about הלל's פרוסבול. It brings a משנה from שביעית that explains what a פרוסבול does and why הלל made it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמיטה cancels debts, so people were afraid to lend as שמיטה came close. That broke the Torah's warning not to refuse a loan for this reason. הלל made the פרוסבול so that debts would still be collectible, and people would keep lending.

keyTerms.meaning: A document that keeps a debt from being cancelled by שמיטה
We learned in a משנה elsewhere

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole discussion of פרוסבול that follows. It shows that הלל's תקנה was made to protect the poor and keep loans going.

phrases.english: Hillel instituted the prosbul, etc.:
We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in שביעית 10:3.

phrases.english: A prosbul is not cancelled.
phrases.notes: He means that שמיטה does not cancel a debt that has a פרוסבול.

phrases.english: This is one of the things
that Hillel the Elder instituted;
for he saw the people
who held back from lending to one another,
and they transgressed what is written in the Torah:
"Beware lest there be a thing
in your heart, a base thought, etc.,"
He arose and instituted the prosbul.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלֵּל הִתְקִין פְּרוֹסְבּוּל וְכוּ׳: תְּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה after finishing the signature discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פרוסבול prevents שמיטה from cancelling a debt; הלל made it because people stopped lending

steps.title: The wording of the פרוסבול
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the text of the פרוסבול: the lender hands his debts to the judges so he can collect whenever he wants, and judges or witnesses sign below.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the main text of the פרוסבול: 'I hand over to you, so-and-so and so-and-so, the judges in such-and-such place, that any debt owed to me by so-and-so, I may collect whenever I want.' And the judges sign below, or the witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and tells us what a פרוסבול actually says. The lender hands his debts over to a בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמיטה cancels debts between people, but not debts held by a בית דין. By handing his debts to the judges, the lender keeps them from being cancelled. The document is signed by the judges or by witnesses.
steps.whatToRemember: A פרוסבול works by handing the debts to a בית דין, so the lender can still collect after שמיטה.

phrases.english: And this is the main text of the prosbul:
"I hand over to you,
so-and-so [and so-and-so], the judges
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added by the corrected wording; some versions don't have them.

phrases.english: who are in such-and-such place,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכׇּל חוֹב שֶׁיֵּשׁ לִי אֵצֶל פְּלוֹנִי,
phrases.english: that any debt owed to me by so-and-so,
I may collect it whenever I wish."
And the judges sign below,
or the witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from שביעית by giving the text of the פרוסבול
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פרוסבול hands the lender's debts to the judges so he can collect at any time; judges or witnesses sign it

steps.title: How can הלל undo a Torah law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the פרוסבול: if the Torah says שביעית cancels debts, how could הלל make an enactment so that it does not?
steps.simpleTranslation: But is there such a thing, where by Torah law the seventh year cancels the debt, and הלל made an enactment that it does not cancel?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the very idea of the פרוסבול. It seems to let a Rabbinic enactment cancel out a Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 17, הלל made the פרוסבול so the debts would not be cancelled. But if the Torah itself cancels debts in שביעית, it seems strange for חכמים to simply undo that. The גמרא wants to know how this is allowed.

phrases.english: But is there such a thing
that by Torah law the seventh year cancels the debt,
and הלל made an enactment that it does not cancel?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the פרוסבול enactment quoted in Steps 17-18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Rabbinic enactment should not be able to undo a Torah law that cancels debts in שביעית.

steps.title: אביי: it is about שביעית nowadays, following רבי
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that הלל's enactment deals with שביעית in our times, and it follows the view of רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is talking about שביעית in our times, and it follows רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. הלל's enactment only works for שביעית in our times, and it matches רבי's opinion, which the גמרא will quote next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי, nowadays שביעית does not cancel debts by Torah law. It only cancels them because חכמים said so. So הלל was not undoing a Torah law. He was adjusting a Rabbinic law, which חכמים are allowed to do.

keyTerms.meaning: And this follows רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the Torah law of cancelling debts is gone forever. He is saying that in our times it is not in force by Torah law, so cancelling debts nowadays is only Rabbinic.

phrases.english: אביי said:
It is talking about the seventh year in our times,
and it follows the opinion of רבי –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the enactment applies only when cancelling debts is Rabbinic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פרוסבול seemed to undo a Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Nowadays cancelling debts is only Rabbinic, according to רבי, so הלל could make an enactment about it.

steps.title: רבי's source: debts are cancelled only when land is released
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי's teaching: the פסוק speaks of two kinds of release, land and money, so when land is not released, money debts are not cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי says, "And this is the matter of the release: release". The פסוק is speaking about two releases, the release of land and the release of money. When you release land, you cancel money debts. When you do not release land, you do not cancel money debts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows רבי's opinion, which אביי relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי reads the double wording of the פסוק as pointing to two releases, land and money, and ties them together. In our times land is not released, so by Torah law money debts are not cancelled either. That is why the cancelling of debts nowadays is only Rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: Release of land (land returning to its owners)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי, cancelling debts depends on releasing land. Since land is not released nowadays, debts are cancelled only מדרבנן, so הלל could make the פרוסבול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how a Rabbinic enactment like the פרוסבול can work. It does not undo a Torah law, because nowadays the law it changes is only Rabbinic.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא, רבי says:
"And this is the matter of the release: release" –
phrases.notes: דברים 15:2. The release is mentioned twice, and רבי reads that as two kinds of release.

phrases.english: the פסוק is speaking about two releases:
one is the release of land
and one is the release of money.
At a time when you release land –
you cancel money debts,
at a time when you do not release land,
you do not cancel money debts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבי's opinion, which אביי cited in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that nowadays שביעית cancels debts only מדרבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי on דברים 15:2, which links the release of money to the release of land
